purpose: Second set: five new African streetwear and contemporary graphic-art webpage concepts, responding to owner's feedback.

concepts.name: Roots & Rebellion
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE extraordinary desktop HOMEPAGE image for ALKEBULAN, a modern AFRICAN STREETWEAR label built around cultural graphic tees. Render a finished website straight-on, landscape 1536 x 1024; no device frame, no wireframe, no moodboard. Hero should dominate 75-85% with the beginning of real shopping content below. This is series TWO: the owner liked the earth and dark palettes of a previous set but specifically rejected its generic luxury-interior feeling. They want this to scream AFRICA + STREETWEAR + CONTEMPORARY AFRICAN GRAPHIC ART. Make the graphic identity unmistakable through expressive Black representation, original rhythmic illustration, bold printmaking, contemporary African fashion styling, image-making and type. Sophisticated but culturally confident, youthful and visually intense. Strong composition and clear usable commerce UI. DO NOT return another decorative niche, clay room, floating-shirt-in-a-ring, quiet luxury serif layout or beige interior photograph.
INPUT ROLES: references 1, 2, 3 are supporting product inserts: the owner's actual Ijele, Durbar, Dùn Dùn black tees. Preserve their exact graphic prints, original lettering, garment cuts and black fabric when displaying them or dressing a model. Do not invent new shirt artwork. Ref 4, a supplied sheet of black and cream abstract graphic FACES, is the key visual-art direction anchor; its powerful cut-paper geometry, expressive faces and print texture should visibly inform the composition. Ref 5, supplied charcoal-and-rust geometric art, is a secondary reference for drawing rhythm and distressed print surface. Use these as contemporary graphic-art references, with no invented claims that any mark is a particular tribe's sacred writing. No arbitrary borrowed logos. Any people are fictional ADULT African fashion-campaign models, never celebrity lookalikes or endorsements.
Readable ALKEBULAN wordmark, clean small navigation 'Collection / Men / Women / Our story', simple search and bag icons, a clear primary shop button. No fake prices, fake discounts, fake testimonials, fake awards, fake dates of founding, fake sold-out stock. Short editorial copy, large typography. No savannahs, safari props, wildlife, tourist imagery, random costumes or historical-artifact displays. Streetwear styling means boxy graphic tees, wide trousers, contemporary jewelry and confident poses, never ceremonial costume. New contemporary illustration can use abstract portraiture and rhythmic marks without claiming historical provenance. No paragraphs of tiny filler. Small precise concept label provided below. Each concept must look like its own creative direction, not recoloring one template.

CONCEPT LABEL: '01 / ROOTS & REBELLION'. A radical earthy AFRO-GRAPHIC fashion poster translated into a premium usable website. Bone paper, burnt terracotta, dense black and a restrained warm brass-yellow accent. Flat matte screenprint texture. Top is a compact black navigation strip with ivory ALKEBULAN wordmark. Main hero: MASSIVE condensed typographic statement 'CULTURE IS THE UNIFORM.' arranged in two broad bands, interlocked with an oversized African graphic-art FACE on the right: graphic head with geometric eye, pronounced nose, asymmetric cheek pattern and braided black line work, clearly contemporary cut-paper modern art related to input 4. Art should cover a major part of the canvas, not a tiny ornamental border. In the center-left, a confident fictional young adult dark-skinned Black male fashion model in the EXACT Ijele tee and baggy washed black trousers, waist-to-knee editorial crop, slight low-angle lens, leaning forward, real flash-lit garment texture. The model and huge block-face art partially overlap the type, but the headline remains readable. A thin hand-printed ochre rhythm band crosses behind the composition, some roughly registered ink gives life. Smaller left-bottom copy 'African roots. Street expression.' A strong black rounded-rectangle 'Shop the collection' button on bone paper. A single terracotta circular arrow seal can punctuate the edge. Bottom starts a clean bone collection rail featuring the THREE REAL tees and readable product names. It must look like a fiercely original African streetwear art-director's campaign: expressive, graphic, cultural, tactile and high fashion. NO architecture, no arches, no museum pedestals, no polite serif hero.
